top_signals.title: Americans Hit Hardest by War-Driven Oil Price Surge
top_signals.summary: Americans are paying the biggest portion of global energy price inflation resulting from the war in the Middle East, a Finnish energy and climate outlet has reported. Estimating the global total in fuel inflation at $468 billion, the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air said the U.S. portion of this total stood at $160 billion. On a per-capita basis, Americans are also paying the most, CREA also said, estimating their additional costs at $471 per person, while the global total has been estimated at an average of $60. top_signals.title: Pimco Would Welcome 2027 UK Fiscal Deficit of Around 3.5%
top_signals.summary: Pimco economist Peder Beck-Friis looks ahead to UK Chancellor John Healey’s budget announcement, highlighting the Office for Budget Responsibility’s (OBR) fiscal deficit forecast for next year as the critical metric for the gilt market. "If that comes in in the mid-threes, I think that will be welcome news for the bond market," Beck-Friis tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Mixed outlook for energy expenditures this winter
top_signals.summary: We expect energy expenditures this winter to vary because of diverging trends in energy prices among fuels and regional variation in forecast temperatures. We expect that lower prices for natural gas and propane will drive decreases in expenditures this year for the half of U.S. households heating with those fuels. Higher prices for electricity and heating oil drive increased expenditures for households heating with those fuels in our forecast.
